objective: Standard statement: among the 742 relations on four bits in which every three coordinates are unconstrained, other than the full cube (complements of nonempty independent sets of the 4-cube), determine (i) which have a coordinate symmetry group inside the rotations of some cyclic order (they orient a vertex), and (ii) which are rebuilt, up to leg order, by native gadgets of two or three of their own copies with four legs, together with the gadget shapes that rebuild them. Prediction from scoping (two copies only): the rebuilt relations are four-bit parity and relations of the form R(x_i + x_j, x_k + x_l) over GF(2) with R a two-place relation (pairwise relations between parities of pairs), none of them orienting a vertex, and their towers are chains. Nearest known result: as in ticket A; classification: no overlap found (candidate local delta).
status: Proved by GEOMETRY-LAW-20261029-001B-P001 (V1, exhaustive census plus prose): among the 106 classes of four-bit knots, native gadgets of two and three copies rebuild exactly the even parity class (every gadget), the odd parity class (odd numbers of copies) and the implication between pair parities (exactly the chains, and chains of every length); every other class loses excluded tuples; 96 relations in 6 classes orient a vertex and none is rebuilt. Larger gadgets are sampled, not exhaustive.
title: Four places: orientation, and which knots survive patterns of patterns
